title: Compliance team weekly
transcript:
Marcus Bell: Okay, let's get started. It's 1:00 on Tuesday the 22nd. Agenda today: AML alert backlog, the KYC pipeline ownership transfer coming on October 6th, the periodic review on c_0067, and the sanctions screening tuning item. Nadia, start us off with alerts.
Nadia Petrov: Thanks. AMLMonitor generated 214 alerts last week, down from 261 the week before. Backlog stands at 38 open alerts older than five business days. Most of those are the structuring-pattern scenario, which is still noisy. Daniel and I have been triaging and about 70 percent are closing as false positives.
Daniel Sanchez: Right, and I want to flag that the noise is partly because FraudScore scores are feeding into the AMLMonitor thresholds, and the DataLake refresh has been lagging by a few hours on some mornings. A couple of alerts fired on stale data and cleared on re-run.
Marcus Bell: Is that something Technology knows about?
Daniel Sanchez: I haven't raised a ticket yet. I'll open one with the data engineering group today and reference the specific alert IDs.
Marcus Bell: Good. Action item, Daniel, ticket on DataLake refresh lag affecting AMLMonitor, by end of day. Nadia, what's your target for the backlog?
Nadia Petrov: Under 15 older than five days by Friday the 2nd. I'd like Anthony to take a handful of the lower-risk ones so Daniel can focus on the two that might become SARs.
Anthony Ramirez: Happy to. I can take ten this week. Do I need a second sign-off for closures?
Nadia Petrov: Yes, anything with a counterparty hit needs my sign-off. Plain false positives on the structuring scenario you can close with a documented rationale.
Marcus Bell: Okay. Let's move to the SARs. Daniel, status on the two?
Daniel Sanchez: One is ready for narrative review. The other, I'm still waiting on supporting documents out of DocVault, and the retrieval has been slow. I think we're fine on the filing deadline but I'd rather not get close to it. The narrative draft goes to Nadia on Thursday.
Marcus Bell: Fine. Nadia, you review by Friday, and I'll do final approval Monday.
Nadia Petrov: Works.
Marcus Bell: Next, KYC pipeline. Linda, Luis, you're closest to this. As everyone knows, ownership of KYCPipeline moves from Operations to Compliance on October 6th.
Luis Bowen: Yeah. From the day-to-day side, the biggest gap is on-call. Right now Operations handles pipeline failures and we just file requests. After the 6th, we're the ones who get paged when screening jobs stall. The pipeline depends on ClientHub, DocVault, and SanctionsScreen, so a failure in any of those looks like a KYC problem to us.
Linda Jones: I put together a draft runbook. It lists the three upstream dependencies and who to contact for each. ClientHub goes to the Wealth Management team, DocVault and AuthSSO go to Technology, and SanctionsScreen is already ours. I still need a section on manual override procedures for onboarding when screening is down.
Marcus Bell: Manual overrides need to be conservative. No client onboarded without a completed sanctions screen, period. If SanctionsScreen is unavailable, onboarding holds.
Linda Jones: Agreed, that's how I wrote it. Holds with a queue and a daily status note to the relationship managers.
Marcus Bell: Good. Luis, do you have a view on who covers on-call?
Luis Bowen: I'd propose a rotation of four of us, weekly, with Heather and Anthony in it along with me and Linda. We'd need training with Operations before the handover.
Heather Carlson: I'm fine with that. Can we get a walkthrough from Ravi's team? I haven't seen the failure modes firsthand.
Marcus Bell: I'll ask Ravi Patel for two sessions the week of September 28th. Action for me. Linda, finalize the runbook by October 2nd and circulate for comments. Luis, draft the rotation schedule by the same date.
Luis Bowen: Will do.
Marcus Bell: Next item, c_0067, the periodic review. Heather, you've got this one.
Heather Carlson: Yes. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0067}} is a commercial client since 2020, medium risk, with an operating account and a loan account. The periodic review is due and we found a mismatch: the address on file in ClientHub, {{CLIENT_ADDRESS:c_0067}}, doesn't match what appears on the latest documents in DocVault. Also the EIN on the file, {{CLIENT_EIN:c_0067}}, needs to be re-verified against the updated corporate filings.
Marcus Bell: Is there any activity concern?
Heather Carlson: Not an alert as such. But there were a couple of larger wires on the operating account, {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00141}}, to a counterparty, Reid-Wilson. The beneficiary details on file reference {{CP_ACCOUNT:cp_039}}. Activity looks consistent with their stated business, but I want the documentation on that relationship in the file.
Nadia Petrov: I looked at those wires last week. Amounts are in line with their history and nothing tripped the monitoring scenarios. I'd say document it and keep medium risk.
Marcus Bell: Agreed. Heather, reach out via the relationship manager, Jasmine Johnson, rather than contacting the client cold. Request updated address proof and the corporate filings. Do it this week with a 10 business day deadline.
Heather Carlson: Will do. I'll note it against the loan account too, since Lending relies on the same file.
Marcus Bell: Good. Last item, sanctions screening tuning. Anthony?
Anthony Ramirez: We're seeing a lot of fuzzy-match hits on common surnames for business entities. I tested lowering the match sensitivity slightly in the test environment, and hits dropped about 18 percent without missing any of our known true-positive test cases.
Marcus Bell: I'm cautious on that. A regulator will ask why we loosened anything. I want a written validation, with a larger test set, and sign-off from me before anything moves in production.
Anthony Ramirez: Understood. I'll write up the methodology and run it against the historical true positives from the last two years.
Marcus Bell: Target October 9th for the document. Anything else? Okay. Summary of actions: Daniel, DataLake ticket today. Anthony, ten alerts this week and the tuning validation by the 9th. Nadia, SAR narrative review by Friday. Linda, runbook by October 2nd. Luis, rotation by October 2nd. Heather, the c_0067 documentation request this week. And I'll set up the Operations sessions. Thanks, everyone.
